verified_findings.story_title: UAA EEG acquisition expands task-specific research capacity
verified_findings.confidence: high for acquisition, hardware and stated plans; no completed-study efficacy claim

fact_check_safe_set.claim: UAA announced the acquisition on September 9, 2026.
The AI and Robotics Lab acquired a Wearable Sensing DSI-24 dry EEG.
The Educational Legacy Fund funded it.
Faculty and students received equipment training; Egorov viewed his recorded signals.
It records scalp electrical activity using 19 electrodes, plus two earclips and three auxiliary inputs.
Reading-task cognitive-state estimation is planned, including participants with disabilities or neurological/developmental conditions.
Programming-task brain-activity and eye-movement research is also planned.
Egorov usually uses public EEG datasets and anticipates collecting task-specific data.
An August workshop lists Egorov presenting supervised transfer learning with S-JEPA for motor-imagery EEG classification.
The manufacturer identifies the device as research equipment, not a clinical or medical diagnostic instrument.
Testing segments from the same people in both partitions can overstate EEG-model performance on unseen people.

verified_quotes.text: so I’m excited to be able to collect my own data for my own tasks
verified_quotes.speaker: Vadim Egorov

allowed_numbers.meaning: Auxiliary inputs, not necessarily attached sensors

explicit_obligations.requirement: Use future/planning language for C6 and C7 in both narration and visuals; a headset acquisition is not a published experiment.
Make acquisition and training the observed milestone. Signal traces may illustrate recording; any model answer must remain an unanswered research target.
Separate measurement, labeling and inference. Scalp voltages do not themselves reveal comprehension, intentions or thoughts.
Do not depict reading people's minds, diagnosis, treatment, or autonomous medical decisions.
Do not describe an AI-assisted coding experiment. The announced task is computer programming; no AI-assistant condition is specified.
Do not present an accuracy rate, sample count, successful classifier, exact purchase date, price, or completed dataset as a reported UAA result.
Keep the earlier S-JEPA presentation separate from new-device research. Do not assign that architecture or QStates to either planned study.
Label held-out-person validation as an editorial methods principle: to claim generalization to new people, test people absent from training. Never imply UAA committed leakage.
New local data enables a relevant test; its collection alone does not prove a model generalizes. Evaluation must match the intended use and population.
Do not attribute institute enthusiasm to Alaska residents generally, or invent participant consent, recruitment, tribal partnerships, or community endorsement.
Use only the short verified quote above from the announcement. Any additional UAA quotation must stay within the same-source quotation allowance.
If 19 sensor points are literal in a graphic, count them; stylized signals must not look like real measured UAA study results.

methods_evidence.finding: The authors tested segment-based versus subject-based data partitions in two EEG datasets and found inflated estimates for unseen-person prediction when identities crossed the split.
methods_evidence.inference_for_story: A distinct person should remain outside training when the claim is performance on new people. This supports a careful closing question, not an accusation or an efficacy claim.
methods_evidence.do_not_import: Clinical conditions, numerical accuracies and cohort sizes in this older methods study are not UAA outcomes.

local_sentiment.assessment: Egorov and faculty express enthusiasm; no independent participant or community reaction verified.

unsupported_claims_cut: Specific QStates or S-JEPA use in the new studies
